transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today; what brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been really struggling with the aftermath of a traumatic event that happened about a year and nine months ago. I keep having these terrible, intrusive memories and distressing dreams about it that I just can't get out of my head. I really need some help figuring out how to deal with this.
Have you been experiencing these intrusive memories and distressing dreams regularly since the event occurred, or did they start more recently?
Yes, I've been dealing with them regularly ever since it happened. They started almost immediately after the event and have been happening consistently for the last year and nine months.
Do you find yourself actively trying to avoid conversations, places, people, or even thoughts that remind you of the event?

Yes, I do everything I can to push those thoughts and memories out of my head because they're just too painful. I also go completely out of my way to avoid certain places, people, and even conversations that might remind me of what happened.
Have you noticed feeling constantly on guard, easily startled, or having trouble sleeping and concentrating since the event?

Yes, I feel constantly on guard and can never seem to relax, always scanning my surroundings for danger even when I know I'm safe. I've also been having a really hard time concentrating or staying focused on simple daily activities.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or how you view yourself and the world, such as feeling detached from loved ones or having persistent negative thoughts?

Yes, my view of everything has changed drastically since it happened. I constantly feel completely damaged and worthless, and I struggle to trust anyone because people just feel dangerous to me now. It truly feels like the entire world is an unsafe and terrifying place.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all DSM-5 criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), including exposure to a traumatic event, intrusion symptoms (memories, dreams), avoidance behaviors, negative alterations in cognitions and mood (worthlessness, lack of trust), and alterations in arousal (on guard, concentration difficulties) lasting for 1 year and 9 months (well over the 1-month requirement). No other diagnoses are suspected, so the interview can be finalized.
